model_organism.citation: Exp. 2023 - Early developmental deletion of forebrain Ank2 causes seizure-related phenotypes by reshaping the synaptic proteome (PMID: 37428632)
phenotypes: Prenatal cortical excitatory neuron and oligodendrocyte deletion (Ank2-/-:Emx1-Cre) caused severe spontaneous seizures
Increased neuronal calcium event amplitude and frequency, network hyperexcitability and hypersynchrony in cortical slices
Upregulation of dendritic spine plasticity-regulatory proteins and downregulation of intermediate filaments in synaptic membranes
Perampanel restored cortical neuronal activity and partially rescued survival
Adolescent deletion (CaMKIIα-Cre) did not produce these phenotypes

model_organism.citation: Kv7/KCNQ potassium channels in cortical hyperexcitability and juvenile seizure-related death in Ank2-mutant mice (PMID: 37321992)
phenotypes: Increased excitability and firing rate of cortical neurons
Decreased Kv7.2/Kv7.3 levels and function with lengthened axon initial segment
Retigabine rescued neuronal excitability, juvenile seizure-related death and hyperactivity

biological.summary: Ank2 is highly expressed in the embryonic mouse cerebral cortex. In utero electroporation knockdown of Ank2 altered neural stem cell differentiation and neuronal migration, and changed the expression of neurodevelopmental genes.

biological.citation: ANK2 autism mutation targeting giant ankyrin-B promotes axon branching and ectopic connectivity (PMID: 31285321)
biological.summary: Giant ankB (a neurospecific ANK2 isoform) localizes to periodic axonal membrane domains via L1CAM. There it couples microtubules to the plasma membrane and prevents microtubule entry into nascent branches. In mice, the ASD mutation or giant ankB deficiency increases axon branching, causes ectopic connectivity and transiently increases excitatory synapses, and produces dominantly inherited social/communication deficits.

biological.citation: ANK2 loss-of-function variants are associated with epilepsy, and lead to impaired axon initial segment plasticity and hyperactive network activity in hiPSC-derived neuronal networks (PMID: 37195288)
biological.summary: CRISPR heterozygous ANK2 LoF hiPSC-derived excitatory neurons showed hyperactive, desynchronized network activity on MEAs. They also had increased somatodendritic complexity, altered AIS structure and impaired activity-dependent AIS plasticity. These findings are coupled with 12 patients carrying de novo LoF variants who have a neurodevelopmental disorder with ID, ASD and early-onset epilepsy.

biological.citation: Physical and functional convergence of the autism risk genes Scn2a and Ank2 in neocortical pyramidal cell dendrites (PMID: 38290518)
biological.summary: Ankyrin-B scaffolds NaV1.2 (Scn2a) to the dendritic membrane of mouse neocortical pyramidal neurons. Ank2 haploinsufficiency phenocopies the dendritic excitability and synaptic deficits of Scn2a+/- neurons.

biological.citation: Giant ankyrin-B mediates transduction of axon guidance and collateral branch pruning factor sema 3A (PMID: 34812142)
biological.summary: AnkB440 acts in the Sema3A signaling pathway by stabilizing the L1CAM/neuropilin-1 receptor complex, enabling growth cone collapse. It also reduces F-actin-rich branch initiation points. ASD-linked ANK2 variants failed to rescue Sema3A-induced growth cone collapse.

biological.citation: Multiple autism genes influence GABA neuron remodeling via distinct developmental trajectories (PMID: 40795403)
biological.summary: In C. elegans, loss of unc-44 (ANK2 ortholog) increased neurite outgrowth of the GABAergic DVB neuron in adults. It also altered DVB presynaptic morphology and impaired DVB-regulated spicule protraction behavior. unc-44 was one of only two genes (with unc-36) hitting both the morphology and behavior screens.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Role of ANK2 in autism
biological.summary: ANK2 mRNA and protein are reduced in patient PBMCs. L1CAM protein abundance is decreased in patients with ANK2 mutations (a translocation and two nonsense mutations). L1CAM expression is rescued by ANK2 transfection into a patient cell line, supporting an ANK2-L1CAM interaction in ASD and agenesis of the corpus callosum.

biological.citation: ASHG 2015 - Integrative Analysis of Human Protein Complexes Reveals Biochemical Activities and Convergent Mechanisms of Action in Autism Spectrum Disorders
biological.summary: Mass spectrometry in neuronal culture purified ANK2 co-complexed proteins, alongside CHD8, CUL3, DYRK1A and POGZ. The interacting proteins formed a network preferentially expressed in early fetal brain. The network showed increased mutational burden in ASD and was regulated by FMRP and MeCP2.

biological.citation: Common genetic variants in ANK2 modulate QT interval: results from the KORA study (PMID: 20031550)
biological.summary: A common ANK2 SNP (rs6850768) shortens QT interval in two population cohorts, as does the rs11098171-rs6850768 haplotype. RT-PCR in human left ventricle identified two novel ANK2 5' exons near the associated variants.

biological.citation: Spatio-temporal expression of ANK2 promotes cytokinesis in oocytes (PMID: 31511568)
biological.summary: Ank2.3 is the only Ank2 transcript variant in the mouse oocyte. Its mRNA is enriched in the nucleoplasm and then the spindle, and is translated after nuclear envelope breakdown via a 5'UTR oligo-pyrimidine motif and a cap-dependent pathway. Blocking ANK2 translation causes oocyte cytokinesis defects.
